difficulty_reason: Counts the author Proposition: for ring maps A -> B -> C there is a canonical distinguished triangle L_{B/A} tensor_B^L C -> L_{C/A} -> L_{C/B} -> ...[1] in D(C) (source lines 1586-1595). The proof applies the derived lower shriek functor to the short exact sequence of sheaves of the triangle short exact sequence lemma, producing a distinguished triangle whose terms are three lower shrieks of differential sheaves; the identification of the second and third terms with L_{C/A} and L_{C/B} uses the computation of the lower shriek along the projections together with the computation of the cotangent complex, while the first term is rewritten using the change-of-rings lemma, the flatness of the sheaf of differentials over the structure sheaf, and again the cotangent complex computation.
